summary: @servicetitan/marketing-email-components preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`, which fires automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs downloads a Bun runtime binary from the oven-sh/bun v1.3.13 GitHub release for the installer's detected platform/arch, extracts it to a temporary directory, sets it executable, and immediately invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` — a 727 KB obfuscated bundle marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` whose logic is driven by a rotated string-array decoder (`n7gIxM` / `WV8StW` / `hc1jfK9`) with no readable identifiers or imports. setup.mjs itself is obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers and per-function property-lookup indirection hiding constants such as `--version` and `/etc/os-release`. Executing the payload under Bun rather than Node keeps the code path invisible to standard npm audit tooling. A React/email-template component library has no legitimate need to fetch a second JavaScript runtime at install time to run an opaque bundle; the shape is alternate-runtime-dropper install-time RCE of author-controlled code the installer cannot audit.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
